end.summary:
Rohan practised defining food miles as the journey from farm to plate.
They used labels such as “Product of China” to identify where food comes from.
They compared local and far foods using travel distance and line length.
They identified fuel use and possible pollution from longer journeys; freshness and cooling needs remained partly explored.
Teach-back was not passed; no misconceptions were recorded.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised reading food labels, comparing local and far foods, and linking longer journeys with more fuel and pollution. They explained the farm-to-plate meaning of food miles and applied it to apples and spinach. Freshness and cooling were mentioned but could be revisited with a simple example. At home, ask Rohan to compare two food labels and draw a short or long journey for each.
